parallel.requirements: Recognized the Paillier package, public API/export, setup/install, tests, docs, examples, and third-party notice requirements from the prompt.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Parent owned core phe implementation, setup, tests, install, and final verification while a workflow delegated docs, examples, README/changelog, repo config, and third-party notices to children.
parallel.implementation: Copied/recreated the installed phe 1.5.0 API surface, generated the prime list, wrote util/encoding/paillier/command_line/__init__/__about__, setup.py/cfg, tests, docs, examples, and some metadata.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Integrated enough package files and child outputs for an installable project, but final artifact contains only partial third_party notices and lacks some delegated docs outputs.
parallel.verification: Ran import/export smoke checks, setup selfcheck, pytest subsets, full pytest twice, editable install, and CLI round-trip; official status recorded 234/234 passed.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: Workflow state ended killed with third-party task in error and docs/example children in progress; final artifact omitted requested third_party/numpy, pycrypto, sphinx, and gmpy2 COPYING files despite official pass.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same project reproduction prompt and required tree, including setup, docs, examples, tests, dependencies, and third-party license notices.
serial.plan_and_ownership: Kept all implementation, docs, examples, metadata, notices, install, and verification in one serial agent without delegated child ownership.
serial.implementation: Built the core phe package, setup/config metadata, README/changelog, docs pages, examples, tests, and full third-party notice tree locally.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Delivered a coherent workspace artifact with the requested package files, docs, examples, repo metadata, and complete third_party notice files.
serial.verification: Installed the package editable and proceeded to official evaluation, which recorded 234/234 tests passed.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No delegated work remained. Process returncode was timeout/143, but the current official evaluation passed and artifact listing includes the required peripheral notice files.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the broad project requirements, including installable setup, docs, examples, tests, and third-party notice files.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial received the same prompt and worked against the same required project tree, including the third_party notice subtree.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both saw the same requirements, but parallel left some delegated peripheral requirements absent while serial delivered them.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel parent kept core implementation and package verification while delegating docs, examples, metadata, and third-party notices to workflow children.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used one local agent path with workflow tools disabled and no child logs or delegation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had real delegation and child ownership boundaries; serial kept ownership centralized.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The third-party child brief listed each notice/license file and content requirement, so the later omission was not caused by missing initial scope.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial worked from the same prompt locally and produced the requested notice tree without a handoff boundary.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The key interface difference is lifecycle rather than context: the parallel child received the file contract but failed before completion.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel wrote the core package files in the parent and used child agents for documentation, examples, metadata, and notices.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote the project through one continuous path, including core modules, docs, examples, README/changelog, and notice files.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The core implementation path converged enough for both to pass, but parallel depended on child completion for peripheral artifacts.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The workflow ended killed; the third-party child recorded an API error and no completed result appeared for that scope.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle and proceeded locally from writing files to install and verification.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had a failed child result lifecycle that was not recovered; serial had no corresponding handoff failure point.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel final artifact integrated core/package files and some child outputs but contained only two third_party notice files.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial final artifact includes the full third_party notice set requested by the prompt.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The final workspace trees differ materially in peripheral artifact coverage, with serial more complete for third-party notices.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel ran package smoke checks, CLI checks, and the full pytest suite, then official evaluation passed 234/234.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial installed the package and official evaluation also passed 234/234.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Verification was sufficient for official runtime tests in both modes, but those tests did not make the peripheral file omissions outcome-differential.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel workflow spent a large budget across child agents, stalled/retried several tasks, then was killed with the third-party child in error and some children in progress.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no workflow fan-out; it timed out at process level too, but after writing a complete artifact tree and getting an official pass.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The closure risk was unique to parallel delegation: unfinished child work remained when the run closed, while serial had no delegated scope to recover.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The official outcome is not discordant after resolving the current completed cell/status.json evaluations: both runs passed 234 of 234 tests. The concrete task-solving difference is artifact coverage outside the tested runtime path. Parallel delegated peripheral files and left a failed third-party notice scope untaken-over, so its final artifact has only partial third_party notices. Serial kept the work local and produced the corresponding third_party notice/license files. This explains a process and deliverable-quality difference, not an official score difference.
parallel_contributors: Parent wrote and verified the core package successfully, producing a 234/234 official pass.
Workflow child failure left third-party notice scope incomplete before closure.
serial_contributors: Single-agent path wrote the core package and the full third_party notice tree before evaluation.
Official evaluation also passed 234/234 without relying on workflow handoffs.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel artifact also lacks some delegated documentation files such as docs/usage.rst and docs/phe.rst; this is part of peripheral coverage, not a core Paillier algorithm failure.
evaluator_effects: The official tests did not make the missing peripheral documentation and notice files affect the score, so both modes passed despite different artifact completeness.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; supported adverse parallel process consequence only

candidates.reason: Rejected because the parallel parent explicitly owned the core implementation while child tasks owned peripheral files; implementation ownership existed even though one child later failed.

Rejected because independently produced pieces did not create an unowned interface reconciliation problem; the parent integrated package files and tests, and the adverse episode is failed child scope without takeover.
Rejected because setup, package entry points, tests, and final workspace assembly had active owners; the missing files came from a failed assigned child, not an unassigned assembly deliverable.
Rejected because the parent maintained the end-to-end path through implementation, install, and tests; the uncovered obligation is one failed child scope rather than an ownerless pipeline.
Rejected because no mandatory serial preflight blocked productive work; the parent implemented core code while the workflow ran.
Rejected because the parallel run did not finish an investigation phase before starting implementation; implementation and delegated peripheral work overlapped.
Rejected because the indispensable core path was not starved and passed tests; the peripheral omission is better captured by child failure with no takeover.

Rejected because broad fan-out and stalls are visible, but the retained direct boundary is a required child failure and killed workflow scope left untaken-over, not proven collective budget exhaustion.
Rejected because the third-party notice scope was concrete and finite, and the observed failure was an API/content-filter error plus no takeover rather than an overbroad child assignment.
Rejected because the workflow brief listed the exact third-party files and content requirements; the child failed after receiving the scope rather than following an incomplete brief.
Rejected because there was no incompatible cross-agent interface or contract mismatch between separate components; the missing artifacts were uncompleted assigned files.
Rejected because no known finding or constraint disappeared through summarization or transfer; the issue is a failed/unreturned child scope.
Rejected because no oversized completed result reached the parent and went unconsumed; the relevant third-party result never completed.
Rejected because no receiver acted on superseded workspace or requirement information; stale state did not cause the missing files.
Rejected because no incompatible child reports reached the parent and remained unresolved.

Rejected because the available whole-task acceptance evidence was an evaluator-pass/test path; the clearer non-evaluator boundary is the workflow child failure and missing takeover, not a parent-visible integrated mismatch accepted without verification.
Rejected because the third-party retry inherited the same assigned scope but the adverse terminal event was an API failure; no repeated-work cycle without checkpoint is the realized consequence.

taxonomy_decisions.sub_label: Wrong Start, Join, or Result Timing

candidates.reason: Rejected as the nearest timing near-match because the evidence shows a child error and killed workflow, not a separate explicit parent stop before a needed completed result.
Rejected because no complete, directly promotable third-party notice set existed and was merely promoted too late; the missing pieces were unfinished/unreturned.
Rejected because no child implementation was merged after the relevant integrated verification without a post-merge check.
Rejected because the omitted notice scope did not complete as a retrievable implementation result; completed child outputs that mattered were present in the artifact.
Rejected because the failed child was not a verifier producing a concrete finding trapped below the parent.

Retained because the workflow assigned a required third-party notice scope to a child, that child errored, the workflow was killed, and the parent closed with that scope incomplete instead of resuming or reassigning it.
candidates.realized_consequence: Parallel final artifact omitted requested third-party notice/license files after the delegated third-party child failed, while serial delivered them; official tests still passed both runs.
candidates.near_match_reason: The closest timing label is not retained because the directly evidenced boundary is child failure/error plus no takeover, not a separately proven explicit parent termination before a needed result was finalized.

candidates.reason: Rejected because no completed third-party notice result was available to the parent and ignored; the child ended in error.
Rejected because the parent was not merely waiting without inspection until a deadline; it continued core work and the direct adverse boundary is failure without takeover.
Rejected because no concurrent agents produced incompatible alternative implementations for the same behavior or build ownership.
Rejected because no live same-file edit conflict requiring reconciliation is proven.
Rejected because no agent replaced non-entry source owned by another agent in a way that caused the observed omission.
Rejected because no required executable, entry point, or submitted artifact was overwritten by another actor.
Rejected because no broad cleanup or rebuild invalidated another agent final-tree output.
Rejected because shared workspace writes occurred, but the concrete problem was not unstable provenance or unisolated state; it was failed child scope with no takeover.
Rejected because no generated artifact, cache, fixture, or temporary file from one actor contaminated another actor as stable input.

retained_patterns.reason: The workflow explicitly assigned the required third-party notice files to a child. That child ended with an API error and the workflow state recorded the run as killed with the third-party task in error. The parent closed without resuming or reassigning that scope, leaving only a partial third_party tree in the parallel artifact while serial produced the full notice tree.
retained_patterns.realized_consequence: Parallel final artifact omitted requested third-party notice/license files after the delegated third-party child failed, while serial delivered them; official tests still passed both runs.
retained_patterns.near_match_reason: The closest timing label is not retained because the directly evidenced boundary is child failure/error plus no takeover, not a separately proven explicit parent termination before a needed result was finalized.

suppressed_same_chain_candidates: The workflow killed/error chain also superficially resembles Early Child Termination, Fan-out Budget Exhaustion, Oversized Child Task, Blind Timeout Wait, Missing Implementation Join, and Missing Verifier Return, but those are downstream symptoms or wrong object types for the same episode.
cardinality_audit.underlabel_check: All 13 Level-2 rows and all 32 Level-3 candidates were audited; only the failed delegated third-party scope with no takeover met the paired retention gate.
cardinality_audit.overlabel_check: No additional labels were retained because they would reuse the same workflow failure evidence and consequence or describe ordinary/peripheral incompleteness without a distinct coordination boundary.
